steps.content: [Syndicate Battlefield]
Twisted storms ravage the streets, unleashing waves of Mania contamination. The city lies in ruins as terrified civilians scatter in panic, desperately seeking shelter.
Yet for the FAC soldiers, these catastrophes are not the most terrifying enemy they face.
Against the rampaging Tide of Ashes, they stand their ground, defending every street as if it were their last.

steps.speaker: Street Thug
steps.content: Go to hell, you Outland mutts! This is all your fault!!
Fsssst— He ignites a Molotov cocktail, sending fresh waves of panic through the crowd.
An armored hand grabs him from behind, knocks him down, and snatches the bottle, extinguishing the flame.

steps.speaker: Street Thug
steps.content: Wh-what are you doing? I'm doing this for DisCity! They're obviously all—ugh!
The soldier lands a solid punch to the thug's face. Even the most good-natured among them has reached his limit.

steps.speaker: FAC Soldier
steps.content: Stop making things worse! What are you doing running around outside at a time like this? Get to a shelter now! The best thing you can do for DisCity is to keep your damn self alive, you idiot!

The subdued man is shoved toward the evacuation line, whimpering as he goes. But the damage is done. Panic has already taken root. Inside the shelter, people instinctively distance themselves from anyone who looks foreign.
Since the Great Expo, tensions between city-states have steadily escalated. Anti-Outland sentiment has trickled down, poisoning even ordinary citizens.
At this rate, the authorities will have no choice but to separate locals from outsiders inside the shelters, just to prevent further chaos.
But where would they find the personnel? In a place like Syndicate, with its constant churn of people—immigrants, descendants, drifters—hoping to avoid violence is a pipe dream.
—If real conflict breaks out, who should he protect?
The hand that struck through his armor burns like fire, even through the protection.
[Enter Flashback]

steps.speaker: Siglinde
steps.content: Sir, if I may. The FAC's core tenet is "protection." But in practice, does that not often mean you're reacting to a threat only after it has already manifested? Wouldn't it be too late?

steps.speaker: Siglinde
steps.content: I'm curious about your view on the principle that "the best defense is a good offense." Why hold to a purely defensive stance? Is it a matter of doctrine... or capability?
[Exit Flashback]

steps.speaker: FAC Soldier
steps.content: Tch... She doesn't have a damn clue...
From a distance, someone in a small vehicle has witnessed the entire scene.
[Different Street]

steps.speaker: West District Staff Member
steps.content: I'm sorry, kid... With things as they are, we can't take you to the Executive Committee to find your mother anymore. There are too many dangerous incidents along the way, and we can't guarantee your safety.

steps.speaker: West District Staff Member
steps.content: There's a shelter entrance nearby. We can head there to take cover and help out while we're at it. Would that be okay with you?
Elvira nods.

steps.speaker: Elvira
steps.content: I'm coming with you.
She tries to appear braver, but as she follows them out of the vehicle, her legs tremble so violently she nearly stumbles.
The rumbling engines, the howling sandstorm, the screech of Manic Entities, the screams and roars of the crowd... She still hasn't adjusted to any of it. But what she just witnessed is worse.

Inside the underground shelter, a clamoring crowd presses into every available space. Some shove anxiously forward; others weep in silence. Many glare with naked hostility. It's impossible to tell who's from DisCity and who's an Outlander—everyone seems to be sizing up the unfamiliar faces in their own way.
In the thick air, heavy with gunpowder, mud, and sweat, Elvira catches a familiar scent.
[Flashback Intercut]

steps.speaker: Street Thug
steps.content: Go to hell, you Outland mutts! This is all your fault!!

steps.speaker: Selyna
steps.content: Don't think I'll fall for your tricks! Go to hell!!!

steps.speaker: Jelena
steps.content: See, Chief? Even those with blood-stained hands can have a heart. They can love. They just choose carefully who deserves their love... That's what DisCity has taught me.
[Exit Flashback]
Her head throbs as if splitting open, but she can't stop now. If she does, everything she's worked for will be wasted.
Where to next? Wait for the clerks to finish and follow them to the Executive Committee to find Matilda Cavendish? Or explore this area and gather more intelligence?
According to this morning's news, Max King is also making a public appearance in a nearby district. If she could meet him again... that might prove useful.
Elvira struggles to think as voices flood her ears—curses, pleas, desperate calls—all blending into a wall of sound.
Until a single name cuts through the noise, sharp and clear.

steps.speaker: Sibilla
steps.content: Wait, kids, don't go! We'll get medicine, but you have to keep yourselves safe right now!

steps.speaker: Sibilla
steps.content: Sable wouldn't want you to put yourselves in danger!
As the staff member finishes clearing the safety entrance, he turns to find Elvira standing in a trance, already moving toward the crowd of refugees.

steps.speaker: West District Staff Member
steps.content: Um, kid, we're already at... Wait! Where are you going?!!

steps.speaker: Elvira
steps.content: ...Sorry, I... I just remembered I have something to do...

Another sudden tremor shakes the ground. Half a wall shears away and crashes down, blocking the path between him and Elvira. In the chaos of falling debris, she seizes her chance and vanishes into the sea of people.
[Scene Change] Alley
Sibilla huddles in a triangular space formed by broken walls, barely sheltered from the onslaught of the Tide of Ashes.

Though she's no stranger to catastrophes, the devastation here—in this "prosperous," densely packed district—far exceeds anything she witnessed in her hometown. It's clear the Syndicans have no experience dealing with disasters of this scale.
She anxiously fiddles with an old mobile terminal in her hands. The Mania storm raging overhead chokes the air with interference, making communication nearly impossible.

steps.speaker: Sibilla
steps.content: Hello? Hello? Ashley? Allen? Can you hear me? Oh, thank heavens, this old thing still works...

steps.speaker: Sibilla
steps.content: Now you listen to me, and you listen good. Don't even think about going out for medicine. You wouldn't know what's out there, and we can't just give Sable anything. Her poor body's too weak as it is, and this is no common fever. Cold medicine won't touch it.

steps.speaker: Sibilla
steps.content: Once I find Gracelyn, I'll be back right away. I'll be counting on you looking after her, alright? Yeah, just wait for me. I'm on my way now—

steps.speaker: Elvira
steps.content: Wait—!

A silver-haired girl emerges from the mouth of the dark alley. She stands poised at the edge of the ruin, dressed in the unmistakable style of Eastside's upper levels—her clothes crafted from soft, lustrous fabric that glimmers with understated wealth.
Sibilla gasps. Her terminal clatters to the ground.
The girl doesn't seem to notice Sibilla's panic. A light sweat glistens on her skin from her hurried chase, and her eyes shine with urgency as she squeezes into the cramped corner.

steps.speaker: Elvira
steps.content: I... I overheard you mention someone named Sable. Is she unwell? Does she need cyborg repairs? Maintenance, or parts... I-I could help!

steps.speaker: Sibilla
steps.content: ...Cy...borg? What?
With a deafening roar, the underground shelter collapses, sending dust billowing everywhere. Reacting on pure instinct, Sibilla seizes Elvira's arm and hurls them both sideways.
